description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

Why Join Us?

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

About the Team

Minerva is STARK’s overarching Mission Operating System — the central cognitive backbone connecting all our unmanned platforms across air, land, and sea, while seamlessly integrating third-party systems and interfacing directly with national Battle Management Systems (BMS). Within this ecosystem, the Minerva Frontline organization owns the entire human-machine interface and operator experience on the ground. Our program brings together three specialized product pillars — Minerva Frontend Applications, Ground Control Stations (GCS), and Mission Simulation — distributed across Berlin and Munich. We operate with high autonomy, a mission-first mindset, and close collaboration between software engineers, hardware specialists, and operational experts to build reliable, intuitive systems that work when stakes are at their highest.

Your Mission

As Director Minerva Frontline, you are the holistic Program Owner and external face of STARK’s customer-facing software and mission control suite. Reporting directly to the VP of Software, you will lead the departments across Command & Control (C2) Applications, Ground Control Stations, and Simulation, unifying their efforts into one cohesive, battle-tested product experience. You will set the visionary product roadmap internally while representing our capabilities externally to military stakeholders, procurement agencies, and partners across NATO nations.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Own the end-to-end Minerva Frontline program, taking full accountability for its strategic roadmap, program budget, commercial targets, and cross-functional delivery across all three product lines.
  • Lead, mentor, and empower three direct reports and scale the broader multi-disciplinary organization across Berlin and Munich in these teams.
  • Define and communicate a compelling product vision internally, aligning engineering and UX teams around operator needs so that software, ground station hardware, and simulation environments feel like one seamless system.
  • Serve as the primary external representative for Minerva Frontline, pitching and demonstrating our C2, GCS, and simulation capabilities to military end-users, defence ministries, and procurement bodies (e.g., BAAINBw).
  • Drive seamless system interoperability, ensuring Minerva Frontline connects effortlessly with STARK’s physical unmanned platforms, third-party assets, and sovereign Battle Management Systems .
  • Translate complex battlefield and customer requirements into structured, actionable engineering priorities, balancing rapid prototyping with mission-critical reliability and safety.
  • Establish and scale a lean Program Management Office (PMO) over time to professionalize program tracking, release planning, and cross-entity alignment.
  • Collaborate closely with Commercial, Marketing, and Physical Platform Leads to shape go-to-market materials, pricing models, and integrated system demonstrations at test ranges and customer sites.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Proven senior leadership and program ownership experience managing complex, multi-team software or cyber-physical product organizations, including responsibility for roadmaps, budgets, and delivery.
  • Strong technical background in building mission-critical software suites, ideally combining software engineering leadership with hardware-in-the-loop, robotics, C2 systems, or ground control interfaces.
  • Credibility and domain expertise in the defence or aerospace sector, with the ability to speak at eye level with military decision-makers, operators, and technical engineers alike.
  • Exceptional internal and external communication skills — you know how to inspire engineering teams with a crisp vision and persuasively represent complex technical products to B2G (Business-to-Government) customers.
  • High organizational rigor and an owner’s mindset, capable of turning startup ambiguity into clear structure and driving execution under high tempo.
  • Willingness to travel regularly between our hubs in Berlin and Munich as well as to customer sites, military bases, and test ranges across Europe.
  • Fluency in English (written and spoken) is mandatory.

Nice-To-Have

  • Prior military service (e.g., former officer or reservist in the Bundeswehr or a NATO allied force), particularly within IT, Cyber, C2, or Air Defence domains.
  • Fluency in German, enabling seamless direct engagement with German defence stakeholders and procurement authorities.
  • An established network within the European defence ecosystem, military procurement agencies, or the NATO technology community.
  • Experience with tactical Battle Management Systems (BMS), military simulation environments, or unmanned systems (UxV) operations.

 

Equal Opportunity:

At Stark Defence, we are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing team. We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We actively encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and identities.

If you are excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the listed qualifications—ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. We value unique perspectives, adaptability, and a drive to solve high-stakes challenges.

Security Clearance:

Due to the nature of our work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate security clearance required for this position. Details will be provided during the recruitment process.

description:
About HelloFresh

HelloFresh Group reaches more than 6 million customers across 16 markets through a portfolio of 8 consumer brands — from meal kits and ready-to-eat meals to pet food and specialty products. HelloTech, our global technology division, builds the digital consumer experience across Berlin, Warsaw, and North America: the apps, the personalization, the discovery moments, and everything in between that turns food into something people genuinely look forward to.

Design is core to how we compete. Our Consumer UX team designs end-to-end experiences across all 8 brands, and we hold a high quality bar — internally, our “zest-appeal” framework defines design excellence from baseline usability through to best-in-class, surprise-and-delight craft. We are also moving fast to an AI-native way of working, where AI rethinks discovery, prototyping, and the path from design to code. Experience quality and innovation are leadership priorities all the way to the group president.

About the role

This year we are doubling down on craft, execution, and design leadership. In a world where it is easier than ever to get software to 75% built, it is the last 25% — the polish, the motion, the detail customers actually feel — that decides whether a consumer experience is merely useful or genuinely loved. Millions of people open our apps every week to feed themselves and their families; the final 10% is the difference between a transaction and a habit.

This is a build-and-scale role, not a maintenance one. We are hiring a design leader to own a consumer experience domain within the Consumer mega alliance, raise the quality bar across it, grow a high-performing team, and build the design-technology and AI-native capability that turns ambitious ideas into beautifully executed, shipped products. We need a maker and a leader who leads through the work — not a strategy-only or people-management-only role.

The level — Director or Senior Director — will be set by the candidate’s experience and the final scope of the domain. We are open to both.

What You’ll Do: The Recipe

  • Lead from the front. Lead, coach, and inspire a multidisciplinary team — UX, UI, content, and localization — across multiple consumer surfaces. Stay hands-on in the work: review designs, jump into critiques, and drive clarity.
  • Turn ambiguity into clarity. Solve problems from first principles, not templates. Help your team make hard decisions, focus on outcomes over process, and install just the right amount of structure and rigour to ship great work at speed.
  • Set and uphold an extremely high craft bar. From UX flow to polished UI — layout, typography, motion, micro-interaction, and visual storytelling. Be the design-quality amplifier who notices the details others miss and pushes work to where it needs to be, coaching the team to our quality tenets.
  • Own a consumer experience domain end-to-end. Take accountability for the quality and delivery of experiences across the customer journey, from problem framing to shipped product across our brands and 16 markets. Drive design excellence through every detail.
  • Build design-technology capability. Champion and scale our design system (Zest) and modern UI foundations. Close the gap between design and engineering through prototyping, design-to-code workflows, and component quality — making design and engineering faster together.
  • Make us AI-native. Treat AI as an active part of how design gets done — accelerating discovery, generating and validating prototypes, and shortening design-to-delivery. Define the quality bar AI-assisted workflows must meet, and help the company rewrite how consumer products get built in the AI era.
  • Partner deeply with Product and Engineering. Align on priorities, make tradeoffs, unblock delivery, and move fast. Advocate clearly and persistently for the right experience, and raise the ambition of the partners around you.

What You’ll Bring: The Ingredients

  • Team leadership. A track record of leading and growing high-performing design teams in product-first, consumer (B2C) companies — hiring, coaching, and developing designers at all levels, from IC to managers.
  • High agency. You thrive in ambiguous, fast-changing environments, push for the right solution rather than the convenient one, and lean in to make things happen without waiting for permission.
  • A bias to ship. Demonstrated success driving teams to ship great software at scale, not just making decks about it — owning execution across a product line and a portfolio of features.
  • Exceptional craft and product taste. Strong visual and interaction sensibility and a high personal bar for detail. You know what great looks like for a consumer audience, and you can help teams get there — across hierarchy, motion, and micro-interaction.
  • Design-technologist mindset. Fluency at the design–engineering boundary: design systems, component architecture, prototyping in code or advanced tools, and a practical grasp of front-end constraints.
  • AI-native practice. You already use AI across the design workflow — for insight synthesis, rapid prototyping, and design-to-code — and have a point of view on scaling it responsibly with a high quality bar. Fluency with tools like Figma, Claude, and similar is expected.
  • Scale and systems thinking. Experience designing and maintaining quality across a multi-brand or multi-market consumer ecosystem, balancing consistency with brand-specific character.

What Success Looks Like

  1. Your team consistently delivers high-quality consumer product work at speed.
  2. You have hired exceptional talent and helped your existing team grow in craft and execution maturity.
  3. Experience quality in your domain is visibly higher — the last 10% is sweated, and it shows in what customers feel.
  4. Product and engineering leaders love partnering with you because you unlock progress and raise the ambition.
  5. Design systems and AI-native workflows in your domain make the whole team faster without sacrificing craft.
  6. You are a key player in shaping how HelloFresh builds consumer product in the AI era — writing new playbooks, not following old ones.

What We Offer: The Toppings

  • Scale and impact. Shape experiences for 6+ million customers across 8 brands and 16 markets.
  • A craft-and-AI-first culture. Leadership that champions experience quality, innovation, and AI-native ways of working from the top of the organization.
  • Real ownership. End-to-end accountability for your domain, with the autonomy to set and raise the bar.
  • Growth. A defined leadership track and the chance to expand scope as the alliance scales.
  • Global collaboration. Work with experienced product, engineering, and design partners across HelloTech’s international teams.

description:
About AlphaSense: 

AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.

About the Team:

The extraordinary AlphaSense Sales team is split into two parts: Financial Services and Corporates. The Financial Services Sales Team focuses on sales to hedge funds, asset management, investment banking, and private equity. Our Corporate Sales Team is verticalized with a focus on the Fortune 1000 in the subsequent sectors: Life Sciences, Technology, Media, and Telecom, Energy and Industrials, Consulting, and Consumer Packaged Goods. Both the Financial Services and Corporate sales teams have Enterprise and Mid-Market sales professionals, and there is an additional corporate team of sales professionals focused exclusively on Investor Relations.

About the Role:

We are looking for an entrepreneurial, driven and accomplished new business sales professional to join our growing Corporate Sales team focused on selling top Fortune 1000 companies. This is an opportunity to join a high growth company and sell an award winning product that is experiencing rapid adoption across all industry verticals. The person in this role will make a significant contribution in the company’s growth and future success.

Who You Are:

  • An Accomplished Sales Professional who is open to sell into Corporate industry markets which could include Life Science, Technology Media and Telecoms, Professional Services, CPG or the Energy and Industrial verticals. You perceive Sales as both an art and science, and clearly can articulate your version of the ‘science of sales’;  what activity leads to success and ultimately what you need to do to consistently hit your targets. Whether the activity is; pipeline building, managing a heavy volume of product trials, or spearheading a complex discussion. Ideally we would like to see you have gained these skills through experience in SaaS sales, preferably focused on financial information and/or research solutions (not a must-have) 
  • Hard-working and possess a ‘never give up’ attitude: We have a highly motivated team and an accomplished culture. We look for people who possess a natural tenacity and desire to succeed. You set the example for work ethic, forward-thinking, enthusiasm, and commitment.
  • Intellectually Curious: You know the right questions to ask and how to uncover business challenges at all levels of an organization from Analysts to C-level executives.
  • Coachable. You will have the opportunity to advance your career through robust training and development programs at AlphaSense. An openness to feedback and desire for constant improvement is key to success here.
  • A Proficient Communicator: You have the skills necessary to explain complex financial data and concepts to a non-financial audience -- and you are comfortable doing this virtually via video, via phone and/or in writing
  • Knowledgeable about the personas we sell into. (Our product is sold enterprise-wide, but we have particular success within; Corporate Strategy, Market Intelligence, Business Development, M&A, Investor Relations and research-related functions.)

What You’ll Do:

  • Cold call, prospect, conduct frequent technical demonstrations and in a full 360 Sales role, targeting corporate  intelligence departments selling into the Corporate vertical markets.
  • Research opportunities, prospect, initiate discussions, build relationships, conduct demos, oversee product trials, and most importantly, close deals! This is an end-to-end new business sales role and no task is too small or too large.
  • Forecast accurately and develop the necessary pipeline to meet/exceed quota.
  • Work closely with our Product Specialist team during trials to ensure client commitment and ultimate purchase.
  • Gather and distribute product feedback from clients and prospects to the sales and product teams to help us continually enhance our product offerings.

AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination.

In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.

Recruiting Scams and Fraud

We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. These scams may involve fake job offers, requests for sensitive personal information, or demands for payment. Please note:

  • AlphaSense never asks candidates to pay for job applications, equipment, or training.
  • All official communications will come from an @alpha-sense.com email address.
  • If you’re unsure about a job posting or recruiter, verify it on our Careers page.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a scam or have any doubts regarding the authenticity of any job listing purportedly from or on behalf of AlphaSense please contact us. Your security and trust matter to us.

description: About EHG EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide. Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company. The opportunity We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas. You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that. Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets. Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US. What you'll own One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland. Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one. In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment. Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves. Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria. Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other. Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities. Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant. Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly. Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow. What we're looking for Core experience Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance. Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one. Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability. Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard. Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects. Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage. The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure. Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely. Especially compelling Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience. Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes. Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end. Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators. Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth. Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required. What we offer Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you. Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.   • Help develop pitch decks, case studies, proposals, and other sales collateral for new business development.
  • Conduct competitive analysis and market research to keep our AI propositions sharp and well-positioned.
  • Contribute to the packaging and refinement of InDomo’s AI service offerings.

Platform & Innovation

  • Become proficient in WPP Open, exploring new features and capabilities and sharing findings with the team.
  • Stay on top of the rapidly evolving AI and marketing technology landscape, surfacing relevant tools, trends, and opportunities.
  • Bring fresh thinking. We value your perspective as someone close to the latest academic research and emerging ideas.

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s degree in Marketing, Business, Digital Strategy, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
  • A genuine, demonstrable interest in AI and its application to marketing or business. You’ve explored AI tools beyond the basics and can talk about what you’ve learned.
  • Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills. You can take a complex topic, break it down, and communicate it clearly.
  • Confident communicator who is comfortable presenting ideas to a room, whether that’s a team meeting or a client session.
  • Excellent written and visual communication. You can structure a compelling deck or write a clear, persuasive brief.
  • Self-starter mentality. You take initiative, work independently when needed, and don’t wait to be told what to do.

Strong Pluses

  • Hands-on experience with AI tools in an academic or personal project context, such as building chatbots, experimenting with LLMs, using AI coding assistants, or working with APIs.
  • Familiarity with concepts like prompt engineering, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, or agent architectures.
  • Previous internship or work experience in marketing, consulting, or a technology-related field.
  • Experience with enterprise platforms (e.g., CRM systems, marketing automation tools, or analytics platforms).
  • Familiarity with Dutch and/or international market dynamics.

What We Offer

As part of the WPP network, you’ll have access to a world-class professional environment and a comprehensive set of benefits:

  • Real, meaningful work on live client engagements with some of the world’s biggest brands. No busywork.
  • Direct mentorship from experienced AI and marketing transformation leaders.
  • Hands-on experience with WPP Open and cutting-edge AI tooling that most people only read about.
  • A competitive internship compensation.
  • Access to WPP’s global learning resources and professional development programmes.
  • Light, open-plan office space with roof terrace, on-site bar, and stunning views over central Amsterdam.
  • This role is based at WPP Amsteldok Amsterdam and requires 3–4 days of on-site work, with the flexibility to work remotely 1–2 days a week.
  • A strong foundation for a career in one of the fastest-growing areas in marketing. High-performing interns may be considered for permanent roles.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role Our lab in Lausanne runs thousands of constructs a week through automated workcells, liquid handlers, and binding instruments. That only works if the instruments are calibrated, the buffers are made, the stock is where the system says it is, and the bench is ready when the scientists arrive. You are the person who makes sure it is. You'll own the day-to-day upkeep of our automation and instruments, run buffer and reagent production, keep the lab clean, safe, and stocked, and lead the rollout of new inventory management and lab operations processes across the lab. This is a hands-on, in-the-lab role, working closely with our Lab Manager, the Lab Operations team, and the scientists whose experiments depend on you getting it right. What You'll Do Run daily and weekly calibration of our Hamilton liquid handling systems. Calibrate and maintain key instruments, including the Echo and pH meters. Look after the SPR system: buffer bottle changes, rinsing, and routine upkeep. Take ownership of our automated workcells and keep them clean, organized, and calibrated. Prepare buffers, reagents, and reaction mixes according to established SOPs. Run weekly buffer production and handle ad-hoc requests from the team. Lead the rollout of new inventory management and lab operations processes across the lab, and help design and improve them as the lab scales. Organize fridges and storage, run inventory, and keep consumables, glassware, and bench supplies stocked so experiments never stall. Keep benches and shared spaces clean, clear, and ready for work every day. Manage hazardous and biohazardous waste disposal (including broken glass and sharps), waste sorting, recycling, and general waste removal in line with safety regulations. Run the lab dishwasher and make sure clean glassware is always available. Plan and document scheduled deep cleans and preventive maintenance. What We're Looking For Laboratory apprenticeship (CFC Laborant/in), BSc in a relevant field, or an equivalent lab technician qualification. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Precision in following and executing protocols and SOPs. A service mindset. You enjoy making other people's work easier. Comfortable with routine, with an eye for ways to improve it. Calm and reliable in a fast-paced, high-throughput environment. Experience with lab automation or liquid handling systems (Hamilton, Echo, or similar) is a plus. Experience with inventory or LIMS tools is a plus. Proficiency in English and French is a plus. Many of our vendors and delivery services operate in French. Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Lead Bid Manager, UK & Ireland

Your Impact

As a Lead Bid Manager, you will lead Axon’s most complex and highest-impact RFP and tender responses, proposals, and other customer-facing selling documents across the UK and Ireland. You’ll be a member of a global team that supports Axon sales worldwide and will serve as the senior proposal execution lead for the region. You will own proposal development from early procurement engagement through submission and evaluation-period follow-up, translating established win strategy into a controlled response plan and ensuring the final submission is compliant, responsive, scorable, customer-focused, and on time. Your strengths in judgment under ambiguity, cross-functional leadership, technical and proposal writing, and compliance discipline will be central to success.

Focused primarily on UK and Ireland public-sector opportunities, you will work closely with Sales, Bid Strategy, Solutions Engineering, Product, Legal, Security, Pricing, Finance, Services, and executive stakeholders. You will personally lead the hardest pursuits while also strengthening regional proposal readiness, reusable standards, coaching, and execution across bids owned by other Proposal Managers. This is an office-based position in the United Kingdom.

What You’ll Do 

Location: hybrid schedule of Monday working remotely, and Tue-Fri in our London office
Reports to: Director, Global Proposals
Direct Reports: N/A

At Axon, the Lead Proposal Manager is the senior owner of proposal execution for the region’s most complex pursuits. You will engage early in the procurement process, establish how the response will be run, make execution and compliance decisions within approved boundaries, and carry the proposal through submission and evaluation-period deliverables. This is a comprehensive individual-contributor role requiring expertise in the following areas:

  • Proposal Planning & Execution: Translate established win strategy into an executable response architecture, including workstreams, assignments, proof collection, review cadence, decision gates, and submission-readiness criteria. Build pre-bid readiness for anticipated strategic procurements with Sales and Bid Strategy. Drive resolution of product exceptions, compliance issues, and proposal commitments through the appropriate approval paths, while partnering with Sales, Bid Strategy, Pricing, and leadership on commercial, account-strategy, and bid decisions.
  • Team Leadership: Lead large cross-functional teams across Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Legal, Security, Pricing, Finance, Services, Proposal Team members, and executive stakeholders. Drive decisions, close gaps, enforce deadlines, adjudicate conflicting review input, and coach Proposal Managers and Specialists to improve execution judgment, compliance discipline, and independent ownership.
  • Project & Compliance Management: Own proposal governance, milestones, compliance traceability, mandatory requirements, forms, schedules, portals, review cycles, final packaging, and submission readiness. Identify and manage disqualification and responsiveness risks, and preserve proposal context through structured handoff of assumptions, exceptions, commitments, and unresolved risks during clarification, presentation, and other evaluation-period activity.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with our EMEA Emerging DNB Solutions Architects, Solutions Engineers, and Account teams to scope, design, and de-risk GenAI use cases — from retrieval-augmented generation and agentic systems to fine-tuning and evaluation.

  • Enable and mentor the broader EMEA Emerging DNB Field Engineering team through workshops, reference architectures, and internal enablement, multiplying GenAI expertise across our ~70-person SA/SE organisation.
  • Represent Databricks externally as a technical thought leader — conference talks (e.g., Data + AI Summit), blogs, and customer executive briefings.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong understanding of the LLM landscape, including leading proprietary and open-source models and providers, with the ability to differentiate their capabilities, trade-offs, and suitability for different use cases, and to articulate a clear, informed point of view (POV) to customers.
  • Deep expertise in the modern GenAI stack: LLM application patterns (RAG, agents, tool use), fine-tuning and model customization, prompt and evaluation engineering, and LLM guardrails/safety.
  • Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, including distributed training, GPU workloads, and the full MLOps lifecycle (tracking, registry, serving, monitoring).
  • Proficiency in Python and the ML ecosystem (PyTorch/Transformers, MLflow, Spark), and comfort building production-quality reference implementations.
  • Experience with the Databricks platform — or the ability to ramp on it quickly — including Mosaic AI, Model Serving, Vector Search, and Unity Catalog. Cloud experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Excellent communication and consultative skills: able to earn the trust of both hands-on engineers and senior technical executives, and to explain complex GenAI trade-offs clearly.
  • A track record of technical leadership and mentorship — someone who elevates the people around them.
  • Comfort operating at the pace of digital-native and high-growth customers, where speed, iteration, and technical credibility win the deal.
  • Based in the United Kingdom and able to work across EMEA time zones, with willingness to travel to customer sites within the region as needed.
  • Background helping digital-native customers build data and ML solutions (e.g., prior experience at a data/ML platform or consulting vendor) is a strong plus.

Nice to Have

  • Public technical presence: conference speaking, published talks, blogs, or open-source contributions in the ML/GenAI space.
  • Domain depth in a regulated or high-stakes industry (healthcare/life sciences, financial services) where model quality, evaluation, and safety are critical.
  • Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to influence roadmap.

Why This Role

You will work on the hardest and most exciting GenAI problems our EMEA Emerging DNB customers have — companies building the future in real time — with the platform and the people to actually solve them, not just advise. You'll shape how one of EMEA's highest-growth business units adopts Generative AI, influence the direction of the product, and build a public profile as a recognised expert in the field. This is the role for a builder and a teacher, who wants their expertise to have outsized impact.

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. description: About the Role Imagine pioneering the mathematical and logical foundations that enable AI to fly safely in real-world, safety-critical aviation. As a Machine Learning Certification Researcher, you will address one of the most fundamental challenges in modern AI: proving that ML models are safe, reliable, and mathematically sound for deployment in autonomous flight. Your work will bridge the gap between cutting-edge statistical learning theory and formal aviation certification frameworks, building upon previous work (EASA CoDANN I and II, and FAA report DOT/FAA/TC-21/48), and putting real-world systems to the test. At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision—developing safety-critical AI systems at the intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, understand, and make decisions in real time, we combine aerospace engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight systems, driving innovation where it matters most. What You'll Do • AI Certification Strategy: Analyze our existing AI certification strategy and help adapt it—or pioneer entirely new strategies—to certify different supervised ML. • EASA Framework Alignment: Connect mathematical guarantees, technical arguments, and model evaluations to the EASA W-shaped process for AI certification in aviation, ensuring our research aligns with the latest regulatory guidelines. • Theoretical Foundation & Modeling: Conduct research into statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and mathematical guarantees for deep neural networks operating under dynamic real-world conditions. • Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistics and stochastic processes to model environmental uncertainties and sensor noise, and to quantify confidence in performance metrics. • Literature & Proof Evaluation: Critically evaluate academic literature, mathematical proofs, and engineering assumptions with peer-review rigor to identify safety limitations and theoretical gaps in state-of-the-art AI. • Regulatory & Audit Justification: Construct robust, logical arguments and technical justifications that translate complex, high-dimensional empirical data into structured evidence for safety audits and certification frameworks. • Algorithmic Validation: Write clean, reproducible code in Python to test theoretical hypotheses, validate certification mechanisms, and benchmark model safety frameworks. Requirements What You'll Need Machine Learning Theory & Mathematics • ML Theory & Statistical Learning: Deep understanding of statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and the mathematical foundations of deep neural networks. • Statistics & Stochastic Processes: Strong background in advanced probability, statistical modeling, and stochastic processes. • Python Engineering: Proficiency in Python with the ability to write clean, reproducible code (can also be learned on the job provided strong theoretical foundations and basic Python coding). Research Rigor • Scientific Research Methodology: Demonstrated capability or background in conducting comprehensive literature reviews, identifying gaps in current state-ofthe-art AI, and synthesizing complex academic concepts into actionable engineering frameworks (can also be learned on the job if you possess a strong quantitative baseline). • Peer Review Expertise: Ability or experience in the peer-review process—capable of critically evaluating mathematical proofs, algorithmic assumptions, and research papers to assess their validity and limitations. Education • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Theoretical Statistics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative research field. Who You Are • Critical Thinking & Healthy Skepticism: You possess a strong spirit of questioning everything. You naturally challenge conventional ML assumptions, probe for hidden edge cases, and refuse to take empirical accuracy at face value without rigorous proof. • Logical Argument Building: You have an exceptional ability to construct robust, airtight logical arguments and technical justifications. You can translate complex empirical observations into structured, defensible evidence that satisfies strict engineering and regulatory scrutiny. • Thrives in Ambiguity: You are motivated by hard, unsolved mathematical problems at the intersection of theoretical computer science, safety engineering, and real-world flight operations Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

Consumer Engagement drives consumer activation, engagement and long-term retention by helping people get more value from Alma. That's because multiple studies have shown that the "Creative" itself is responsible for half of sales lift online, higher than reach, targeting, brand, & recency combined. But creative impact has always been the least analysed and least understood component of a complex set of marketing variables.

This is the problem CreativeX is focussed on solving. We're an end-to-end solution to ingest, process, and analyse content at scale. We help brands isolate creative elements so they can be analysed against downstream ad impact metrics, from clickthrough rates to brand lift.

Our objective is to help marketing organisations power every creative decision with data.

Product Design Team

You'll be the design lead in a product trio alongside a Product Manager and an Engineering Lead, owning whether users want what we build and whether they can figure out how to use it, while sharing discovery, outcomes and trade-offs with your partners.   • Experience working closely with Product and Engineering in a product trio or small team, with real ownership

description: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role This is not a lab technician position. This is a senior scientist who owns assay quality, data QC and controls, and production troubleshooting across the entire experimental pipeline. The production team runs 150+ experiments per month across expression, BLI, SPR, thermostability, and enzyme activity. When something goes wrong (failed expression, anomalous binding data, instrument artifacts), this person diagnoses the root cause and fixes it. As the assay and instrumentation portfolio expands, this person translates new R&D methods into production-ready protocols, builds robust methods that junior technicians can execute reliably, and designs comprehensive controls that enable automated QC and data processing. This is a player-coach position. You will still run experiments personally, especially as you integrate into the lab, but you will also elevate the whole team's capabilities. What You'll Do Troubleshoot production failures across the full pipeline. A batch of proteins isn't expressing: is it the construct design, the expression system, or the media? BLI sensorgrams look noisy: is it the sensor tips, the sample prep, or an instrument issue? You figure it out, fix it, and make the cause easier to identify next time. Develop and document SOPs for new assays as the portfolio expands. Take methods from the R&D team and make them production-ready: robust, reproducible, and executable by junior technicians without hand-holding. Mentor a growing production team. Set quality standards, review data, train new hires, and build a culture where people flag problems early instead of hiding them. Work at the intersection of biology, automation, and QC. Collaborate with researchers, laboratory technicians, and automation engineers on protocol optimization for work cells, and with software on LabOS protocol integration. Own the relationship between assay science and throughput. The easy version of every assay doesn't scale, and the scalable version often sacrifices quality. You find the right tradeoff. What We're Looking For Deep hands-on expertise in protein production: expression (E. coli, mammalian, cell-free), purification (IMAC, SEC), and biophysical characterization (BLI and SPR at minimum). This isn't negotiable. You need to have done this work yourself, at volume. PhD in protein biochemistry, biophysics, or structural biology, plus 3-5 years in a production or development role at a CRO, foundry, or high-throughput lab. Academic postdocs count if the work was high-throughput and production-oriented. Experience with high-throughput workflows. You're comfortable with 96-well plates and liquid handlers, not just single-column purifications. You've optimized protocols for scale, not just for one perfect result. Mentorship mindset. You've managed or trained junior scientists before. You enjoy teaching and get satisfaction from watching your team grow. Troubleshooting instinct. When data looks wrong, your first impulse is to understand why, not to rerun the experiment and hope it works. Quality-obsessed but pragmatic. You care deeply about data quality, but you also understand that production has deadlines and sometimes "good enough" is the right call. Bridge between R&D and production. You can speak both languages: the exploratory mindset of research and the reproducibility demands of production. The Electrical QC Inspector ensures that electrical systems, components, and installations comply with safety and quality standards. The role includes conducting inspections, testing, and documenting results to verify that work meets project requirements, codes, and industry standards.
  
Key Functions:

  • Inspection of Electrical Installations: Inspect electrical systems and installations during and after the construction process to ensure compliance with safety regulations, project specifications, and industry standards (e.g., NEC, IEC).

  • Testing and Verification: Perform a variety of electrical tests (e.g., continuity tests, insulation resistance tests, voltage tests) to verify the functionality and safety of installed systems.

  • Collaborate with Site Engineers: Work closely with engineers and contractors to resolve quality-related issues and ensure work is executed according to project specifications.
  • Safety Compliance: Ensure all electrical work is performed safely, adhering to workplace safety standards and relevant electrical codes.
  • Inspection of Materials: Inspect incoming electrical materials, ensuring that components meet specified standards and quality levels before being used in installations.
  • Continuous Improvement: Provide feedback and suggestions for improvements in processes, materials, and quality control systems.

Necessary requirement of the Quality Control Inspector:
  

  • A strong Trade/Construction background and/or a third level qualification in Electrical/Mechanical Engineering.

  • Commitment to working to the highest possible standards and delivering high quality results.
  • Proficient in the use of MS office, BIM 360 Field Management or similar platforms.
  • Data Centre, Pharma or similar experience.

  
  
Desired competencies / special roles requirements
  

  • Experience in Electrical Testing & Commissioning
  • CompEx Ex01-04 training
  • Experience of working on HV/MV systems. ‘Authorised person’ experience

Dein Profil

  • Du arbeitest qualitätsorientiert, selbstständig und bringst ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative mit.

Seit 1957 sind wir Vorreiter in den Bereichen Design, Engineering und Projektmanagement. Von der Beratung bis hin zum Bau und der Compliance unterstützen unsere multidisziplinären Design- und Ingenieurteams Unternehmen auf der ganzen Welt dabei, ihre Projekte auf die effizienteste, kostengünstigste und nachhaltigste Weise zu realisieren.

 

Benefits

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten im Rahmen eines Gleitzeitmodells mit Blockzeiten
  • Europäische Projekteinsätze möglich

description: About EHG EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide. Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company. The opportunity We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas. You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that. Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets. Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US. What you'll own One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland. Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one. In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment. Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves. Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria. Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other. Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities. Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant. Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly. Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow. What we're looking for Core experience Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance. Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one. Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability. Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard. Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects. Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage. The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure. Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely. Especially compelling Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience. Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes. Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end. Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators. Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth. Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required. What we offer Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you. Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland. The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth. description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion.

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

Requirements

  • You've spent 5+ years in applied ML or ML research, and you've trained, evaluated, and shipped models that make real-time decisions (ranking, recommendation, bandits, pricing, or LLM routing) and you can tell that story with receipts.
  • Strong Python and SQL at scale: you can pull, clean, and interrogate millions of request-level records without waiting on anyone.
  • You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.
  • You have real opinions about what LLM benchmarks measure, agentic harnesses included.
  • You know enough serving reality (TTFT, decode speed, batching, prefix caching, concurrency) to model the objective honestly.
  • You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.
  • A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

  • You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.
  • Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.
  • You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

  • Own the routing model end to end: features, objective, training, calibration, and release cadence. Iterate it like a product, not a research artifact.
  • Build the evaluation that gates every change: production-parity benchmarks, router-vs-router comparisons, holdouts by task family, error bars on pass rates.
     Nothing ships on vibes.
  • Turn fleet data into training signal: per-request outcomes from production, benchmark rollouts, and override feedback, with failure categorization (infra vs
     task) so poisoned labels never reach the policy.
  • Model the objective the user actually experiences: task success × token cost × wall-clock speed under the real concurrency regime, with cached-input
     economics in the picture.
  • Run the online loop: shadow, A/B, full rollout, drift monitoring, retrain. When production disagrees with your offline eval, you find out why before the next
     ship.
  • Push the frontier where it pays: calibrated decisions, abstention under uncertainty, speed-aware routing. We experiment on what a router should be, not just
     which model it picks today.
  • Partner with platform engineers on instrumentation: the features and labels recorded per request (decode speed first-class among them) and the experiments
     the data path must support.

What’s in it for you?

  • Competitive salary (depending on the level of experience).
  • Enjoy a flexible, remote-first global environment.
  • Collaborate with a global team of cloud experts and innovators, passionate about pushing the boundaries of Kubernetes technology
  • Equity options.

  • Spend 10% of your work time on personal projects or self-improvement. 
  • Learning budget for professional and personal development - including access to international conferences and courses that elevate your skills.
  • Annual hackathon to spark new ideas and strengthen team bonds.
  • Team-building budget and company events to connect with your colleagues.
  • Equipment budget to ensure you have everything you need.
  • Extra days off to help maintain a healthy work-life balance.

Hiring process

  • Technical interview (system design)
  • Live coding

Senior Data Journalist

Weekly office requirement: Hybrid, 2 days in office
Employment type: Permanent

At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for a Senior Data Journalist to play a key role in our PR & Comms team in London. If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.


As our Senior Data Journalist, you’ll:

Play a pivotal role within the PR & Corporate Comms team, interrogating GWI data and transforming it into actionable, commercially impactful and, editorially punchy narratives. With a journalistic mindset, your work will showcase the value of GWI’s solutions across key personas, verticals and, companies to support GWI’s positioning at the forefront of AI-powered insights in an increasingly agent-driven world.


A few things you’ll be responsible for: 

  • Support proactive pitches and media enquiries with data points to strengthen the story and build trust with media partners.
  • Partner with the Marketing and PR team to deliver narrative and unique view points for events through relevant formats and channels
  • Collaborating with Head of Comms, lead on the development and upkeep of industry wide data story tracking and wider press narrative trends, themes and forward features.
  • Partner with Marketing, GWI leaders and Insights team to identify strategic thought-leadership themes and bring them to life through compelling data stories.
  • Partner with the Marketing team to support ABM and demand gen efforts for high-value prospects by transforming GWI data into bespoke insights that drive engagement and accelerate pipeline through tailored content.
  • Build bespoke data stories for high-value accounts, enabling Marketing and Revenue teams to deliver personalized campaigns and outreach that resonate with target prospects.
  • Deliver outputs including presentations, white papers, reports, podcasts, interviews, op-eds and joint deliverables with clients or partners.
  • Ensure all thought leadership demonstrates ROI for target audiences by connecting directly to their workflows and jobs-to-be-done.
  • Represent GWI on global stages—at conferences, client events, panels, and round tables—as a confident and credible spokesperson.
  • Act as an ambassador within GWI and occasionally as a spokesperson for press, championing the narratives we take to market.


It’s also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.


What do I need to bring with me? 

You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:

  • Expert analysis and storytelling skills, with the ability to turn data into insights that directly address media enquiries and client challenges.
  • Adaptability to engage diverse audiences—from research specialists to commercial leaders—always bringing the room with you
  • Experience in PR strategy and media/journalist relations.
  • Strong presentation and writing skills, with the confidence to deliver hour-long sessions,co-present, and field challenging questions on the spot.
  • Deep experience with quantitative research methods and mastery of GWI’s data and software.
  • Solid understanding of GWI’s competitive landscape and future as the human intelligence for the AI era.
  • Proven ability to work independently, managing the end-to-end process of thought leadership creation.

Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.


Why Join Us

  • Influence the global narrative of a fast-scaling company with ambitions to define an emerging category.
  • Work alongside senior executives and cross-functional leaders where your impact is visible at the highest levels.
  • Enjoy a fast-paced, growth-oriented culture with opportunities to make your mark and grow your career as the company scales globally.

 

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion 🫶

Diversity is fundamental to who we are—as a data company and as a workplace. Our data reflects global realities, and so must our teams. We strive to build a workforce as diverse and inclusive as the insights we deliver.

As a Disability Confident employer, we welcome applications from disabled candidates and are committed to making adjustments throughout the hiring process—whether that's extra time, materials in advance or a different format, breaks, an adjusted interview format, assistive tools, or flexible scheduling. We're happy to discuss whatever would work best for you.

We actively encourage applications from underrepresented and marginalised communities.

At GWI, you'll find a place to contribute meaningfully, grow professionally, and belong fully.

description:
About the role

HelloFresh is reorganising UX to work AI-native — practitioners either go deep as platform and skills experts, or broad as generalists who move fluidly across product, design and engineering to drive experience quality and innovation. This role leads UX for our Operations organisation: the part of the business that bridges technology with physical fulfilment, procurement, quality assurance and supply chain, across every market and brand we operate in.

You'll take over from a Director who spent two years shifting this function from reactive delivery to a high-leverage, AI-native strategic partner — including building an internal design platform, integrated with AI tooling, that other parts of the business have since adopted. You inherit that trajectory, not a finished product: some of our highest-stakes bets for 2026, including how we plan menus algorithmically at scale and how we run the internal tools that power supply-chain decision-making, are still being actively designed, not maintained.

This is a Berlin-based, in-person leadership role. Operations is one of several major, Berlin-anchored parts of our technology organization, and regular physical presence — with peers, with your team, and in the room for cross-functional decisions — is a deliberate requirement of how we want this function led going forward.

What you'll own

  • UX strategy and quality across four core areas of Operations: menu planning and food systems (algorithmic menu planning, ranking, demand forecasting, assortment), fulfillment (production, order management, inventory, logistics, manufacturing, supplier reliability), an internal operations-research platform that runs dozens of optimization models across the supply chain, and the technology backbone that keeps our warehouses and production sites running.
  • Continued build-out of an AI-native design practice: extending our design system directly into AI-assisted workflows, and using that as proof that UX can lead — not just support — the company's AI-first agenda.
  • Service design for the internal-facing tools that operators, planners and analysts depend on every day — often the least glamorous and highest-impact surface area in the company.
  • Talent leadership for a distributed team spanning multiple geographies: hiring, career development, and consistent design-quality standards.
  • A seat at the Operations leadership table, partnering directly with the senior Product and Engineering leaders for the organization, and representing UX's interests in company-wide strategy.

What we're looking for

  • 10+ years in UX/product design, including several years leading design for complex, operational, or B2B/enterprise-grade systems — supply chain, logistics, marketplace operations, or similar domains are a strong plus.
  • A track record of shifting a design function from reactive delivery to strategic, AI-native practice — not just familiarity with AI tools, but experience redesigning how a team works because of them.
  • Experience building or scaling design systems/platforms that other teams adopt, and comfort operating at the intersection of design, product and engineering.
  • Strong stakeholder management — this role sits at the table with senior product, engineering and exec leadership and needs to hold its own there.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and unglamorous domains: this is service design for internal operators and planners, not consumer-facing polish, and the highest-value problems here are rarely the most visible ones.

Location & ways of working

Based in our Berlin office, with an expectation of regular in-person presence — this is one of the small number of senior UX roles at HelloFresh where onsite leadership is a deliberate requirement rather than a preference.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people.

At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

Why Join Us?

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.
ABOUT THE TEAM

You will join our Open Source Aero Simulation team, dedicated to building and scaling next-generation autonomous flight systems. We focus on developing, validating, and implementing end-to-end aerodynamic and flight dynamics workflows built primarily on open-source tools and simulation frameworks. By integrating cutting-edge AI agents with open-source platforms, we accelerate rapid prototyping, multidisciplinary design optimization, and mission-critical aircraft analysis. We operate in an agile, hands-on environment where open engineering and cross-disciplinary innovation drive everything we build.

YOUR MISSION

As a Senior AI & Flight Dynamics Integration Engineer, you will own and develop an AI-driven autonomous aircraft design and optimization workflow at STARK. You will integrate LLMs and AI agents with aerodynamics, CFD, flight dynamics, and multidisciplinary simulation tools to accelerate rapid prototyping and aircraft development. Your mission is to automate complex engineering decision-making loops and deliver highly performant, software-defined flight platforms.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Develop LLM and AI Agent-based engineering workflows to interpret aircraft requirements and support iterative design decisions.

  • Automate parametric aircraft geometry using OpenVSP, Python, and STEP-based CAD workflows.

  • Integrate Flow5 (VLM / Panel Methods) and OpenFOAM CFD to build aerodynamic databases including C_L, C_D, C_m, C_p, and stability derivatives.

  • Develop 6-DoF flight dynamics and flight mechanics models, including trim, stability, control authority, propulsion, and aircraft performance calculations.

  • Integrate aircraft KPIs such as take-off/landing speed and distance, range, endurance, rate of climb, and efficiency into an automated optimization loop.

  • Drive multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO) frameworks to rapidly evaluate aircraft trade-offs.

  • Collaborate with systems and software teams to validate dynamic models against simulation and flight test data.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant professional experience in engineering automation, aerodynamics, or flight systems.

  • Strong background in Flight Dynamics, Aerodynamics, and Stability & Control.

  • Demonstrated experience with Python and engineering workflow automation.

  • Hands-on experience with OpenFOAM, VLM/Panel methods, or OpenMDAO.

  • Degree in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Systems, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Direct knowledge and experience with OpenVSP and Flow5.

  • Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs, AI Agents, and modern MDO tools.

  • Experience in unmanned aerial systems (UAS) or rapid-prototyping defence environments.

 

If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, and you see yourself reflected on the description above, please send us your CV in English. We´re looking forward to meeting you!

 

Equal Opportunity:

At Stark Defence, we are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing team. We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We actively encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and identities.

If you are excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the listed qualifications—ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. We value unique perspectives, adaptability, and a drive to solve high-stakes challenges.

Security Clearance:

Due to the nature of our work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate security clearance required for this position. Details will be provided during the recruitment process.
